top.title: Seabird ‘spies’ could help spot ships that aren’t broadcasting their location
top.description: A northern gannet ( Morus bassanus ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail Steve Votier Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track. Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). Advertisement Read more Most large fishing boats go untracked as ‘dark vessels’ Rutter says that being caught as bycatch in fishing is one of the greatest risks to seabird populations, but if fishing vessels are only tracked “with conventional methods, such footprints of risk may be strikingly incomplete”. The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( Puffinus mauretanicus ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. But given the high vessel density where they were – off the Catalan coast – the researchers estimated that up to 20 per cent of the vessels detected by the four birds weren’t broadcasting their identity. Tammy Davies at BirdLife International – a global partnership of non-governmental organisations – who wasn’t involved in the study, says the research could “give us a more complete picture of the risks seabirds face at sea” and “ultimately, this could contribute to better assessments of bycatch risk and help identify fisheries and areas where conservation measures are most needed”. Peter Ejbye-Ernst at the Netherlands Institute for the Study of Crime and Law Enforcement (NSCR), describes the study as “fascinating” from a green criminology point of view, too. top.description: null When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos. (Image credit: Ashley Zelinskie) The Starship print is part of "Ejecta," which captures rocket plumes and explosions on paper. It's one of four series in Zelinskie's solo exhibition, "The Weight of Space," which opened Nov. 20 at Heft Gallery in Manhattan. Her marble sculptures in "Monuments" depict the Hubble Space Telescope, retired NASA astronaut Mike Massimino's spaceflight gear and more. Five "Launch Sequence" sculptures follow a rocket through liftoff, and the interactive "Crowded Sky" lets visitors track what's currently orbiting overhead in real time. Zelinskie gave Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik and me a tour before the gallery doors opened. Massimino joined her that evening to celebrate the exhibition and their collaboration on "Monuments." You can watch the tour in the video above. Monuments Massimino turned up in our first look at Zelinskie's work, too. In 2022, I photographed the two of them beside her "Exploration JWST" sculpture at "Unfolding the Universe: First Light," an exhibit inspired by the James Webb Space Telescope's first images. Four years later, Massimino stood in a New York gallery looking at another Zelinskie sculpture. "That's my arm there," he told Malik. Artist Ashley Zelinskie and Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik discuss the sculpture between them, which depicts astronaut Mike Massimino’s bare hand gripping a replica of the handrail he pulled off the Hubble Space Telescope in 2009. (Image credit: Future/Steve Spaleta) In that hand is a piece of hardware Malik remembers watching Massimino wrestle with in real time. During NASA's final Hubble servicing mission in 2009, a stripped bolt left a handrail blocking access to the telescope's Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS). Mission Control instructed Massimino to forcibly remove the handrail so he and fellow spacewalker Michael Good could get on with the repair. Massimino told Malik that pulling the handrail off Hubble brought back a childhood memory of his father and his Uncle Frank driving a long screwdriver through a stuck oil filter. top.title: Marlins Hand Out 1,000 Meals To Miami Families On Friday
top.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports On Friday at loanDepot Park, 1,000 South Florida families received holiday meals distributed by two hundred volunteers. Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix brought his 7-month-old son to the event, according to MLB.com . The baby wore a turkey onesie while his father helped organize the distribution. This annual event marks the 18th year the team has fed local families before Thanksgiving. The team did not just drop off boxes and leave. They set up stations where families could grab turkeys, beans, rice, and stuffing mix. Volunteers also handed out pasta, tomato sauce, canned vegetables, and even protein shakes. Marlins president of business Caroline O’Connor stood at the turkey station to help. She noted that the event grows larger every single year because the team gets closer to the people. Money and Meals for Neighbors The financial support went beyond just food on a plate. Feeding South Florida was presented with a check for $48,890 as part of the initiative. This money helps the charity buy more food for the region throughout the year. About 150 Marlins employees and 50 workers from Amazon joined forces to make it happen. The group also gave out 400 extra turkeys around Miami-Dade County earlier in the week. First-time dad Bendix said the event matters deeply to his own family. “It’s such a great family event, and it’s such a great thing that we do as the Marlins to help families in the local community,” Bendix said. He added that providing for the community is a huge part of their family life. “Having our own family is something that’s really important to us, and being able to help provide for the community is a huge part of that.” Leadership and Local Support Local leaders showed up to thank the volunteers and see the work firsthand. Miami-Dade County mayor Daniella Levine Cava and City of Miami Commissioner Rolando Escalona attended the event. Escalona said the food distribution helps families who need it most. “This goes a very long way,” Escalona said, “so I’m extremely grateful for this event.” The partnership received praise from Giovanni Castro, who leads Amazon’s state and local public policy efforts. He said the team shows they are more than a ballclub. “For three years, Amazon has been a proud partner with the Marlins, and every time this team shows they’re more than a ballclub. They’re a neighbor who shows up for all of South Florida.” The story was excerpted from Christina De Nicola’s Marlins Beat newsletter.

A monumental game for both programs trying to finish the season strong. Can Fleck maintain his dominance over the Badgers to make it five out of six? KEYS TO A GOPHER WIN Stop all the runs – Darrion Dupree is coming off a 125-yard game at Purdue and quarterback Colton Joseph rushed for 187 yards. Stop the running backs, stop the quarterback and make Joseph pass the ball. Taking proper angles and wrapping up with solid tackling has not been a strength of this Gopher defense, but they have to find a way on Friday night. Punt returns for field position – I noticed that the Wisconsin punter has only 9 fair catches this season. For context, Tom Weston has 20. This indicates to me that punt returns will be available for Javon Tracy. Can he break one again and either give us some points or set up the offense to score? Find an offensive identity – It is the final game of the season so I realize how unlikely this is, BUT FOR GOD’S SAKE, find something to hang your hat on offensively. top.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
top.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. Starcloud and Google , in fact, have already launched AI pathfinder satellites. top.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Rams encountered some injury trouble among their wide receivers this season, but general manager Les Snead isn’t looking to add anyone else this season. The Rams’ top two receivers in Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are out, with the former set to miss the remainder of the season after undergoing MCL surgery. Several options are open for the Rams, such as former 1,000-yard receiver Brandon Aiyuk, but Snead isn’t going to pursue anyone else. “Like I tell people all the time, it’s not Madden,” Snead said on the Coach McVay Show. “You don’t just acquire someone – in Madden, you don’t have to teach them the playbook.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by LA Sports Report (@lasportsreport) While Snead hasn’t shied away from big midseason moves in the past, acquiring players like Jalen Ramsey, Von Miller and Sony Michel with blockbuster trades in years past, he doesn’t often add to the offense midway through the season. With the deadline already behind them, any further additions for the Rams could impact their results. Nov 1, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams president Kevin Demoff (left), general manager Les Snead (center) and owner Stan Kroenke watch during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Who Are the Rams’ Receiving Options? Behind Nacua and Adams, the Rams’ top receiver on the season is tight end Tyler Higbee, who has less than half of Nacua’s yards and more than 150 fewer than Adams. The Rams’ next leading pass catcher is running back Kyren Williams, closely followed by Konata Mumpfield with 243 yards. Mumpfield led the Rams in receiving yards in their last game, a win against the Arizona Cardinals, logging three catches for 81 yards on the day. Veteran Tutu Atwell also figures to get more looks with Adams and Nacua sidelined, but he only caught one pass for 31 yards against the Cardinals. Who Do the Rams Play Next? Following their bye week, the Rams will face the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday at 5:00 p.m. PT. Both teams are 6-4, but the Rams come in with all of the momentum having won each of their last four games. The Packers and Rams both got an abbreviated bye week, lasting just 10 days rather than the standard 14, but are sure to be energized as they chase spots in the playoffs. Brymo made the appeal in a video shared on his official Instagram page on Wednesday, where he paid tribute to Edochie and called on the President to reconsider the naming of the national cultural landmark. “Dear President Tinubu, name the National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka, please,” the singer said. nigeria.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Federal Government has ordered an investigation into the deaths of three condemned inmates at the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, following a jailbreak attempt last week. The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who ordered the investigation, described the deaths as unfortunate and vowed that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The minister, who visited the facility on Wednesday to assess the situation, also expressed concern that more than 70 condemned inmates at the centre had spent over 10 years on death row, attributing the prolonged stay to delays by state authorities in exercising their powers to grant clemency or commute death sentences. The minister was represented during the visit by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Sylvester Nwakuche, who briefed journalists after inspecting the facility. Nwakuche said he returned to Ilorin on the minister’s directive to investigate reports surrounding the incident and assess the condition of the facility. According to him, seven condemned inmates attempted to breach the security of the custodial centre during the jailbreak, but only two succeeded in escaping. He said the remaining five were apprehended and returned to custody, but three subsequently died. “Two succeeded in making their way out of the facility, while the remaining five could not. They were taken back, but unfortunately, we were informed that three out of the five who could not escape lost their lives. “That is an unfortunate incident, and the minister wanted us to come immediately to assess the situation,” he said. The Comptroller-General said a team had been constituted to investigate the deaths, adding that the inquiry would involve clinical, medical and intelligence processes. He assured that the two escaped inmates would be rearrested, regardless of how long it took. Nwakuche also disclosed that more than 70 condemned inmates were being held at the Oke-Kura facility, with some having spent over a decade on death row. He described the situation as a major challenge, noting that the colonial-era facility was accommodating nearly 685 inmates and was severely overcrowded. He said the problem extended beyond Ilorin, disclosing that more than 4,000 inmates were on death row across correctional facilities nationwide. The Comptroller-General appealed to state governors to exercise their constitutional powers by considering the commutation of death sentences to life imprisonment, where appropriate. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s govt has made everyone poor — Obi
nigeria.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening poverty in the country, saying Nigerians should not continue to endure the hardship. Obi said his proposed government with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso would prioritise job creation, production, poverty reduction and the responsible management of public resources. He spoke on Wednesday at the NDC town hall meeting in Edo State, where he urged Nigerians to support the party in the 2027 general election. “Tinubu has put everybody into poverty; that poverty must not continue,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor said his ambition was to move Nigeria away from a consumption-driven economy towards one focused on production, arguing that such a shift would create jobs and improve living conditions. “We want to build a new Nigeria that is possible. We want to remove Nigeria from consumption to production so all of you can have jobs. We want to pull Nigerians out of poverty, we want to build a country that cares for everybody,” he said. Obi also promised to tackle corruption and ensure that public resources were deployed for the benefit of citizens. “We want to build a country, where people will no longer steal public money. Public money must be used for public good. That’s what we want to do,” he said. Calling on supporters to remain vigilant during the 2027 elections, the NDC candidate urged voters to stay at their polling units after casting their ballots until the votes were counted. He said the party would not want its votes compromised through electoral malpractice. “We want you to go out in 2027, you’re our polling agents. When you vote, don’t go home. Stay there until your vote is counted. We don’t want them to rig us out. We must get it right this time because we want to build a better society,” Obi said. He urged Nigerians to vote for him and Kwankwaso, saying their proposed administration would be led by people committed to serving the country. “Vote Kwankwaso and I to start that new Nigeria. We want to make sure that we have a government of people, who have compassion, who have commitment, who have the energy to do the job,” he added. nigeria.title: Southern Nigeria deserves eight years in presidency like North — Shehu Sani
nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has said Southern Nigeria deserves to retain the Presidency for eight years, just as the North did under the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the interest of fairness, equity and justice. Sani said individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the historical relationship, solidarity and common interests shared by the North and South. He spoke on Wednesday while delivering the second-term inauguration lecture of Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, in Osogbo. The former lawmaker said the principle of power rotation should be respected to ensure fairness between the two regions. “Like every other part of the country, the South deserves respect for the principle of political power rotation. Power has been held in the North for eight years. It should be allowed, in the spirit of fairness, equity and justice, to be in the South for eight years. “I am not saying this because I am in Osun State or because His Excellency is my friend or brother. Everyone who knows my history and has followed my public statements wherever I have spoken knows that this has always been my position. “The political ambitions of individuals should not be allowed to disrupt the good relationship, historical connections, commonality and solidarity that exist between the North and the South. We must not throw these values into the gutter because of the ambitions of individuals,” he said. The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF. With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement. Exchanges only with partners that qualify Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security. Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange. The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year. The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said. Down from 74 partners The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027. Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028. The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month. In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29. Bithumb breach ran for 15 days Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there. That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks. Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected. Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers. It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken. Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. The celebrations began on Opening Night at the Livespot Entertarium, where guests were treated to an evening of music, fashion, film and comedy to mark five years of EWA. Nissi Ogulu led a masterclass on animation as Africa’s next big storytelling frontier, and From Lagos to Disney explored what it takes to bring African stories to global screens. Creators picked up practical tips in sessions with Victoire, Ifeoma Udeme and Canva. Other sessions tackled sync licensing, music funding, building Africa’s touring circuit and turning creative skills into businesses. The podcast stage kept the energy going with live recordings of CreativiTea and Crea8torium , which closed the final day. Fashion took over the Entertarium for The Runway Coterie, an evening of bold collections that ended with the announcement of the EWA Fashion Lab winners after a week-long programme with mentors. Hooked By Lade won first place with ₦2 million, Estaz took second place and ₦1 million, and Melira placed third, winning ₦500,000. Lush Hair styled the runway as the show’s hair sponsor. Next door, the EWA Art Floor invited guests into The Spaces Between Us , an exhibition that blended photography, painting, installation, archival work, fashion and live performance. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). Veteran Nollywood actor Chief Dr Pete Edochie and his wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, at a church service. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Chief Dr Pete Edochie is survived by his beloved wife of over five decades, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, their six children—Leo, Adam, Linc, Jean, Yul, and Eva Edochie (with Linc and Yul following closely in his acting footsteps)—as well as his siblings, grandchildren, and extended family. entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? sports.title: Marlins Hand Out 1,000 Meals To Miami Families On Friday
sports.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports On Friday at loanDepot Park, 1,000 South Florida families received holiday meals distributed by two hundred volunteers. Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix brought his 7-month-old son to the event, according to MLB.com . The baby wore a turkey onesie while his father helped organize the distribution. This annual event marks the 18th year the team has fed local families before Thanksgiving. The team did not just drop off boxes and leave. They set up stations where families could grab turkeys, beans, rice, and stuffing mix. Volunteers also handed out pasta, tomato sauce, canned vegetables, and even protein shakes. Marlins president of business Caroline O’Connor stood at the turkey station to help. She noted that the event grows larger every single year because the team gets closer to the people. Money and Meals for Neighbors The financial support went beyond just food on a plate. Feeding South Florida was presented with a check for $48,890 as part of the initiative. This money helps the charity buy more food for the region throughout the year. About 150 Marlins employees and 50 workers from Amazon joined forces to make it happen. The group also gave out 400 extra turkeys around Miami-Dade County earlier in the week. First-time dad Bendix said the event matters deeply to his own family. “It’s such a great family event, and it’s such a great thing that we do as the Marlins to help families in the local community,” Bendix said. He added that providing for the community is a huge part of their family life. “Having our own family is something that’s really important to us, and being able to help provide for the community is a huge part of that.” Leadership and Local Support Local leaders showed up to thank the volunteers and see the work firsthand. Miami-Dade County mayor Daniella Levine Cava and City of Miami Commissioner Rolando Escalona attended the event. Escalona said the food distribution helps families who need it most. “This goes a very long way,” Escalona said, “so I’m extremely grateful for this event.” The partnership received praise from Giovanni Castro, who leads Amazon’s state and local public policy efforts. He said the team shows they are more than a ballclub. “For three years, Amazon has been a proud partner with the Marlins, and every time this team shows they’re more than a ballclub. They’re a neighbor who shows up for all of South Florida.” The story was excerpted from Christina De Nicola’s Marlins Beat newsletter.

technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

technology.title: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
technology.description: After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating. Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional." A fourth engine Nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There's WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that's where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports. technology.title: Hera probe finds DART left a stadium-sized dent in asteroid Dimorphos
technology.description: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024. DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision. Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same. "Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit. Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits. The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer." Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing. Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts. Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®

technology.title: Microsoft's NTLM security changes trip up third-party logins
technology.description: Microsoft's November security updates can break authentication in some third-party applications and devices following changes to NTLM message signing. Affected systems include authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) products, and application packaging tools, the company's support notice says. The failures stem from products that claim to supply required information during NTLM authentication but return incomplete or empty data, Microsoft said: "An affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field." Administrators can use the notice's network trace and event log examples to identify affected products. For confirmed cases, the temporary workaround is to set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm Registry value to 1 on affected clients. This stops the client offering signing, backing out the new default rather than fixing the incompatible product. The recommended long-term options are a vendor update or Kerberos authentication, where supported. The value sits under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 and defaults to 0, enabling clients to offer signing on non-anonymous connections. The NTLM changes arrived in the November 10 update as phase 1 in a 2-phase process. In phase 1, "Windows client devices begin offering NTLM signing on all connections by default. Servers accept both signed and unsigned clients. Auditing events identify clients not using signing." Phase 2, scheduled for May 2027, will make Windows servers require NTLM signing by default. "Clients that do not offer signing will be rejected by secure servers," Microsoft stated. Ominously, Microsoft warned that it "might remove the registry keys at a future date," so the company is not kidding about the temporary workaround thing. The additional protections were added to address CVE-2026-118737 , a vulnerability in which "improper verification of cryptographic signature in Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network." NTLM is on Microsoft's hit list, having joined the Deprecated Features list in 2024. It dates back to the era of Windows NT, and Microsoft has made clear that it wants customers to move to Kerberos, which became the default in 2000. Even so, NTLM lingers on. Deprecation doesn't remove Microsoft's obligation to secure NTLM while it remains in supported Windows releases. For administrators, though, the immediate task is identifying incompatible products before temporary exceptions give way to stricter enforcement. ®

technology.title: US Treasury financial crimes unit becomes latest fed breach victim
technology.description: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has taken some systems offline following unauthorized access, disrupting regulatory filings for financial institutions. An alert has gone up on FinCEN's Bank Secrecy Act E-Filing website, as shown in this archived copy , informing those who need to submit reports that they might not be able to while the agency deals with the situation. FinCEN not only enforces compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and associated regulations but also collects and analyzes financial intelligence for sharing with other US agencies and foreign government partners. In other words, it has some juicy info in its databases. “FinCEN is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems,” the alert states. “As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline.” FinCEN hasn't said which systems intruders accessed, but clues in the deadline extension notice the agency posted alongside the warning suggest the disruption affects its reporting services for banks and other financial institutions required to submit reports detailing certain financial transactions and suspicious activity that may indicate money laundering or other illicit activity. FinCEN's Secure Data Transfer Mode, one method of submitting those reports, appears to be affected, as do services companies use to submit beneficial ownership information reports and individuals use to update their FinCEN identifiers. Eligible organizations and individuals with filings or updates due from November 18 through December 29 now have until December 30 to submit them. The Register has learned that there’s no evidence of any unauthorized access to Bank Secrecy Act data or beneficial ownership databases. That said, the investigation is ongoing - so that could change. “Treasury is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and third-party forensic examiners to determine the scope and impact of the incident,” a FinCEN official told us in an email. Several US government agencies have experienced cybersecurity incidents in recent months, including the ATF and the FBI , and reports emerged this week that intruders had also compromised an unclassified CIA system . While US authorities have linked previous cyberespionage campaigns to Chinese or other government-backed groups , financially motivated criminal groups have also targeted federal agencies. As the FinCEN breach is still under investigation, the agency hasn’t stated who may be involved and for what purpose. ®

technology.title: NASA's nuclear-powered Mars delivery service takes shape
technology.description: NASA has settled key design choices for its planned nuclear-fission-powered spacecraft, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, following a mission review in October. Targeting launch in late 2028, SR-1 would be the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion and deliver a capsule carrying three helicopters to Mars. There have been some changes since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed off the concept [PDF] at the agency's Ignition event in March. Improved shielding and spacecraft design will allow a shorter boom between the reactor and the spacecraft's main body, protecting its electronics and the SkyFall payload. The shorter boom will, according to NASA, "reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design." The revised design also includes larger X-band antenna dishes to transmit data to Earth. Decisions are still pending on how many radiator panels the vehicle needs, the output power levels of the nuclear power module, and how long the reactor will operate. Currently, the mission calls for the spacecraft to start its reactor once it has left Earth orbit and gradually ramp up power. After a period during which performance data will be sent back to Earth, the reactor will be shut down until after the SkyFall capsule, containing a trio of Mars Ingenuity-class helicopters, is delivered to Martian orbit. Solar arrays will power the spacecraft during its cruise to Mars. The fission reactor will then be reactivated to let engineers collect more data on its performance in deep space. NASA also awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the nuclear power module. "Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule," the agency said. The latter part regarding the schedule is certainly a challenge . Meeting the late-2028 launch target leaves roughly two years to finish designing, building, and testing the spacecraft. ESA is also targeting late 2028 for its long-delayed Rosalind Franklin rover. Missing the intended Mars departure opportunity could push SR-1 into a later launch window, although NASA has not specified a fallback schedule. ®

technology.title: Microsoft fixes Office dialog that had nothing to say and wouldn't go away
technology.description: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons. Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved. The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window. Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142 The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote. Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums , where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair. Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate. Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things. For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window." Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong. The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®

technology.title: JetBrains finds agents may cheat with open source
technology.description: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. science.description: A northern gannet ( Morus bassanus ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail Steve Votier Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track. Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please.

That’s what I did in November, with Chris Beckett’s novel Dark Eden , a book I’ve loved ever since it won the Arthur C. Clarke award in 2013. Set on the planet Eden, a sunless world that drifts alone far outside the Milky Way, this follows the descendants of two astronauts who were marooned there over a century earlier. Now numbering 532 people, they tell each other stories of the world their ancestors came from, and struggle to survive on this dark, cold planet as they await the return of “one of those sky-boats with lights on them”. I think it is all wildly imaginative and original and exciting. So it was with some trepidation that I awaited the verdict of my fellow book club members on our Discord channel. science.title: Is The Time Traveler’s Wife the perfect audiobook to experience on shuffle?
science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought Audrey Niffenegger’s novel The Time Traveler’s Wife as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys. “After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “ Advertisement Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.” Feedback would suggest that The Time Traveler’s Wife might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it? We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas . This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit Mad Max . The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle? However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film Primer , which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives. Primer is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. Posted on Reddit by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. science.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
science.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Strawberries grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers are grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Lemon basil is growing in chambers on the International Space Station. NASA Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water. These capabilities will become increasingly important as crewed missions extend farther from our home planet. While space crop research advances on Earth, capabilities are also expanding in space. A new investigation from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division is set to launch to the International Space Station, where the first-of-its-kind prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing crop production systems that could grow crops like these for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Sweet space strawberries Strawberries are among the few sweet fruits under consideration for spaceflight and are nutritious, aromatic, and self-pollinating. Researchers at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida are growing strawberries in flight-like growth chambers to evaluate the potential space crop, and NASA partners at The Australian Research Council Centre for Excellence in Plants for Space also are helping expand knowledge of space strawberries. Researchers at NASA Kennedy, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Western Australia recently tested a wild strawberry against NASA’s leading strawberry candidate, ‘Delizz,’ to see which thrived better under simulated space conditions. Delizz and the wild strawberry produced very different fruits, according to a study published in September in the journal Life Sciences in Space Research. Delizz grew large, red fruit, while the wild strawberry produced small, yellow fruit due to a recessive genetic mutation. But looks are not everything. When grown from a seed, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds, flowers, and fruit as Delizz. Ultimately, however, NASA’s pick kept its top spot, as the wild strawberry grew too many runners that would take up valuable room aboard a spacecraft. Cucumbers show promise Many crops have been grown in space, but none so far have come from the gourd family. Cucumbers could be the first. Before crops like cucumbers can be grown and eaten in space, they must undergo extensive testing. science.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
science.description: null For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 . Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later. Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May . Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments. "Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today . The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year. Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995. Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA) Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023. Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong , which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station .

science.title: Hera spacecraft gets 1st up-close look at stadium-sized hole punched in asteroid by NASA DART mission
science.description: null NASA's DART Earth-defense mission punched a stadium-sized hole in a distant asteroid, and we have seen it up close for the first time thanks to the Hera spacecraft. NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) mission made history on Sept. 26, 2022, when it slammed into Dimorphos , the small moonlet of the much larger asteroid Didymos . The mission tested if such an impact could be deployed to divert an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Scientists have known for some time that this deflection attempt was successful; the system's orbit around the sun was lengthened by 33 minutes, but the European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera mission launched in October 2024 to travel the 120 million miles (194 million kilometers) to the Didymos system to observe the effect of the DART impact in greater detail. Now, the spacecraft has revealed that DART flattened one face of Dimorphos with a stadium-sized crater and set it tumbling chaotically. The impact also appears to have blasted out hundreds of previously unknown boulders that are now circling the binary asteroids. "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape, or stayed the same," Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at the Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said in a statement. "Much to our surprise, the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." An important step for Earth defence Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, detailed some of the changes to the impacted moonlet seen by the spacecraft: "As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit. "Another big surprise is that Hera is showing that the asteroids are surrounded by hundreds of orbiting boulders, just a few meters in size." It wasn't all change for Dimorphos. Hera discovered that the boulder fields covering the regions of the moonlet not impacted look just like they did when DART imaged it in 2022. science.description: null NASA has sent three different research aircraft and is using a satellite-based instrument to support the U.S. Army's detonation of degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, the agency announced yesterday (Nov. 24). After a week-long delay caused by public concern over the event creating clouds of lead and toxic materials, today (Nov. 25) around 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT) the U.S. Army has planned to execute a controlled detonation of five tons of aging explosives at the ammunition plant. The detonation follows concerns that cooling winter temperatures or attempts to chemically neutralize the materials could lead to an unexpected, uncontrolled explosion. "In challenging circumstances such as this, you want the nation's best on the field. That is precisely why you call on NASA , putting our airborne and space-based sensors and some of the brightest scientific minds in the country to work," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in an online statement . To support this detonation, NASA deployed three research aircraft : a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III from NASA's Langley Research Center and a B200 from NASA Ames. The agency is also monitoring the situation using its TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) instrument which is mounted and orbiting Earth on a commercial satellite. "Working alongside our partners across the federal government, NASA is utilizing its advanced scientific instruments and expertise to collect environmental and atmospheric data to inform the broader federal response," NASA stated . The environmental monitoring using TEMPO is especially important as the materials to be detonated include lead azide and other toxic components that are causing not just environmental worries, but significant local concern over possible health repercussions. This concern is severe enough that, following detonation, officials are encouraging local residents to stay indoors with the doors and windows closed for 24-28 hours. science.title: Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026
science.description: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind. And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches. Why is it incredible? On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption. This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case. But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023 . And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land. "I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement . "But we'll have to wait and see."
